name: Germanium
occurrence: Rare and dispersed; recovered as a by-product of zinc ore processing and from certain coals.
majorUses: Fiber-optic cable lenses and infrared optics
Early transistor technology (before silicon took over)
notableCharacteristics: Was the semiconductor material used in the very first transistor in 1947, before the industry largely shifted to silicon.
whyHere: Sitting directly below silicon with the same four valence electrons, germanium forms the same tetrahedral bonding network — and was in fact the material used to prove semiconductor transistor technology could work at all.
didYouKnow: Clemens Winkler's discovery of germanium in 1886 confirmed Mendeleev's 'eka-silicon' prediction so exactly — atomic weight, density, and all — that it was one of the strongest early validations of the periodic table itself.
genZNote: The OG transistor material before silicon stole the spotlight. Still out here in your fiber-optic cables.
